headline_marked: [[51st death anniversary of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman today]]
headline: 51st death anniversary of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman today
summary: Today marks 51 years since Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and most of his family were brutally killed by a group of renegade army personnel on August 15, 1975.
details: Today, August 15, marks the 51st death anniversary of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. On this day in 1975, he was brutally killed by a group of renegade army personnel at his Dhanmondi 32 residence, an event considered one of the most heinous and brutal assassinations in history.

Alongside Bangabandhu, his wife Begum Fazilatunnesa Mujib, three sons Sheikh Kamal, Sheikh Jamal, and infant Sheikh Russell, and daughters-in-law Sultana Kamal and Rosy Jamal were also killed. His only brother Sheikh Abu Naser, Colonel Jamil (who rushed to save him), SB officer Siddiqur Rahman, and army personnel Syed Mahbubul Haque also lost their lives.

On the same night, another group of army personnel attacked the residence of Sheikh Fazlul Haque Moni, Bangabandhu's nephew and then a youth leader, killing him and his pregnant wife Arzu Moni. Additionally, Bangabandhu's brother-in-law Abdur Rab Serniabat, his daughter Baby, son Arif Serniabat, grandson Sukanta Babu, Serniabat's elder brother's son Sajib Serniabat, and a relative Abdul Nayeem Khan were also killed in a separate attack.

Bangabandhu's two daughters, Sheikh Hasina and Sheikh Rehana, survived as they were in Brussels, Belgium, at the time. Twenty-one years after the assassination, the Awami League, led by Sheikh Hasina, came to power in 1996, initiating the trial of the killers. August 15 was declared National Mourning Day and a public holiday.

On November 8, 1998, a court sentenced 15 individuals to death in the Bangabandhu assassination case, with the High Court later upholding the death sentences of 12 accused. So far, six of the accused have been executed, one has died abroad, and five remain fugitives.

The Awami League returned to power in 2009 under Sheikh Hasina's leadership, ruling for nearly 15 and a half consecutive years. During this period, the party observed month-long programs centered around August 15 and the August 21 grenade attack. Tributes were paid to Bangabandhu's portrait at Dhanmondi 32 and his grave in Tungipara.

However, the political landscape changed with the mass uprising in July 2024, leading to the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government. Consequently, the public holiday for Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's death anniversary, which was canceled last year, is no longer observed.

On August 5, 2024, during the mass uprising, Bangabandhu's residence at Dhanmondi 32 was set on fire and vandalized. Six months later, the house was attacked a second time and subsequently demolished.

In the late 1960s, despite many prominent politicians, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's leadership qualities propelled him to the forefront. Through a long struggle based on nationalist politics, he became the undisputed leader of Bangladesh's independence movement. His historic March 7, 1971, speech at the then Ramna Racecourse (now Suhrawardy Udyan) served as an inspiration for freedom fighters during the war, where he declared, "This time the struggle is for our freedom, this time the struggle is for independence."

headline_marked: [[River erosion threatens Ashashuni homes and market]] in Satkhira, residents helpless
headline: River erosion threatens Ashashuni homes and market in Satkhira, residents helpless
summary: Homes and businesses along the Marichchap River in Ashashuni Upazila are rapidly succumbing to erosion, with residents losing their properties and facing an uncertain future. The situation is exacerbated by recent river excavation.
details: The Marichchap River in Ashashuni Upazila, Satkhira, is experiencing severe erosion, threatening numerous homes and businesses along its banks. Parts of the riverbank have collapsed, and residential structures are showing cracks, with some already lost to the river.

Minara Begum, a resident, has lost three rooms of her house to the river in the past year. Her family's home, built by her husband a decade ago, is now on the verge of being completely submerged, leaving them feeling helpless.

Local residents attribute the increased erosion to the river's re-excavation approximately two years ago. They claim the excavation changed the river's flow, directing strong currents directly towards Ashashuni market and adjacent residential areas.

Mohammad Abdul Hai, a tea stall owner in Ashashuni market for 23 years, notes that the river, once distant, is now perilously close to the market. He states that improper soil management during excavation, where soil was removed from the base of the banks, has weakened them.

Current efforts to prevent erosion, such as placing geo-bags and old sandbags, are deemed insufficient by locals compared to the scale of the problem. Abdul Hai's own home is cracking, with tidal water entering, and he fears it could collapse at any moment.

Ashashuni Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Shyamnanda Kundu acknowledged river erosion as a major problem, affecting not only Marichchap but also other areas. He mentioned ongoing geo-bag placement near Ashashuni market, but noted limited allocation hinders the work.

Satkhira Water Development Board (WDB) Deputy Assistant Engineer Abdul Alim stated that the Marichchap River was re-excavated according to schedule and design. He confirmed geo-bag placement is underway as an emergency measure for about 200 meters, but rain is causing delays.

Alim added that 200 meters of work is insufficient, and a demand for work on approximately 600 meters of the river in the area has been submitted. He hopes that with sufficient allocation, the remaining necessary work can be completed.
